name: Purushottama Perumal Temple, Uthamarkoil
deity: Vishnu as Purushottama Perumal, reclining, with the Goddess Poornavalli Thayar — in a Trimurti temple that also shelters Shiva and Brahma
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Uthamarkoil near Srirangam, Vishnu reclines as Purushottama Perumal with Poornavalli Thayar, in a rare temple that also holds Shiva and Brahma — a Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Uthamarkoil, also called Thirukkarambanur, lies on the northern outskirts of Tiruchirappalli, a few kilometres from Srirangam. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams in Chola Nadu, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; Thirumangai Alvar praises the Lord here as "Karambanur Uthaman" in a single pasuram. The temple is attributed to the Cholas and is administered today by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. Tradition recalls that Thirumangai Alvar stayed in this village for a time while overseeing renovation works at nearby Srirangam. Shiva and Brahma are worshipped here as well, which is why the temple is also remembered as Bhikshandar Koil.
sections.architecture: The temple is raised in the Dravidian manner, with the sanctum under the Udyoga Vimanam. Purushottama Perumal reclines in bhujanga sayanam, facing east, and Poornavalli Thayar has her own shrine. Uncommonly, the complex gathers six sannidhis: Vishnu and his consort, Shiva as Bhikshatana with Parvati, and Brahma with Saraswati. The temple tank is the Kadamba Theertham, and a Kapala Theertham is also named in local tradition.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Shiva, having cut off one of Brahma's heads, was bound to carry the skull as a begging bowl, and no alms could fill it. At Karambanur, Lakshmi, here known as Poornavalli, "she who fills", filled the bowl and freed him from the burden; hence Shiva is worshipped here as Bhikshatana. Tradition also holds that Vishnu stood here as a kadamba tree, so that Kadambanur became Karambanur, and that Brahma worshipped there and bathed in the Kadamba Theertham. The name Uthamar comes from Purushottama, the highest of beings.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the major Vaishnava observances, notably Vaikunta Ekadashi, along with the festival days of the Alvars; because Shiva and Brahma are also worshipped here, their observances are kept within the same precincts. Confirm the festival calendar locally, as dates follow the Tamil almanac.
sections.experience: A rare chance to worship the three deities of the Trimurti beneath one roof, in a calm temple close to the busier crowds of Srirangam. Many pilgrims come after Srirangam, and the reclining Purushottama, the shrine of Poornavalli Thayar and the quiet tank reward an unhurried visit.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi is the busiest day. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Uthamarkoil lies on the northern outskirts of Tiruchirappalli, about 4 km from Srirangam. Tiruchirappalli Junction and Tiruchirappalli International Airport are the nearest rail and air gateways; local buses and autos reach the temple by road.
